risks.note: Management lists tender outcomes and project execution delays among the factors causing fluctuations, and states that the High-Tech segment's lower FY26 revenue contribution primarily reflected the timing and execution of orders. Reducing this volatility through a broader customer base, a wider product mix and scaling of Green Products is explicitly named a management priority.
risks.risk: Revenue volatility from lumpy, tender- and order-timing-driven High-tech segment sales

risks.note: The Company's moat rests on an in-force patent portfolio and proprietary process know-how; management flags both patent expirations and technological obsolescence as threats. In a business where value is converted from IP into licensing and product premium, expiring or superseded patents directly erode pricing power and the out-licensing revenue stream.
risks.risk: Patent expiration and technological obsolescence in an IP-led business model

risks.note: Management states that elevated energy prices and the inflation outlook raise the risk of higher PVA and other input costs. PVA is the core raw material for the Watersol film business, so the pass-through ability against fragmented competition determines segment margin.
risks.risk: Input cost inflation, particularly PVA and energy

risks.note: The importation of non-standard materials, including extruded films from China, continues to pressure competitive pricing in the mass-market segments the Company addresses - notably the embroidery film market it is targeting - capping realisations in the very segments intended to add volume.
risks.risk: Import competition from low-cost non-standard materials, including extruded films from China

risks.note: Management states currency volatility affects both export realisations and imported input costs. With distribution across Europe, Asia, North and South America and Africa and supply points in India, the UK and South America, the exposure is two-sided and structural.
risks.risk: Currency volatility on export realisations and imported input costs

risks.note: Working capital employed increased during the year, reflecting movement in receivables and inventory, and its normalisation continues to be a management focus - a cash-conversion drag on an otherwise debt-free balance sheet.
risks.risk: Working capital absorption from receivables and inventory

risks.note: Management names geopolitical developments among the factors that may cause operational fluctuations; the MD&A macro review points to a Middle East conflict that reset the global outlook, higher trade barriers, deeper geopolitical fragmentation and renewed trade tensions as dominant downside risks.

Security products are supplied primarily to paper manufacturers and require specialised production capabilities, and the Company states it cannot disclose detail on the high-security business because of confidentiality requirements stipulated in its contracts. This limits both diversification and external verifiability of that revenue stream.
risks.risk: Concentration in a small, confidential, contract-bound security customer base

currentContext.expansion: AGTL states it is expanding capacity and diversifying its product offering through capital expenditure, with the green portfolio the focus. The Company holds an industrial plot admeasuring 3 acres in the Dahej-II Industrial Estate in Gujarat, which is intended to support future capacity expansion, particularly in green technologies; the Chairman describes this as an acquisition of land that positions the Company to scale the green segment meaningfully in the years ahead. The existing water-soluble film facility at Ankleshwar, Gujarat sits on land held under a 99-year renewable lease from the Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation and includes an on-site R&D centre equipped with modern instrumentation, with common utilities available to support future expansion. In the High-tech segment, the Security division states it has invested significantly in advanced manufacturing technologies and plans to extend its market reach globally, beginning with exports to the EU and EEA regions; Avery Pharmaceuticals and the Watersol division are targeting expansion into Europe, South America and Africa. Avery Pharmaceuticals operates a WHO-GMP-approved facility at Sanand, Gujarat with German-designed machinery and an in-house product development centre, and is pursuing product registrations in Russia, Yemen and Vietnam alongside CDMO projects. Management says the debt-free balance sheet and liquidity position provide the capacity to fund the Dahej expansion and further R&D investment without external leverage. No commissioning date, ramp timeline or rupee project cost is disclosed anywhere in this bundle.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Management lists tender outcomes and project execution delays among the factors causing fluctuations, and states that the High-Tech segment's lower FY26 revenue contribution primarily reflected the timing and execution of orders. Reducing this volatility through a broader customer base, a wider product mix and scaling of Green Products is explicitly named a management priority.
- The Company's moat rests on an in-force patent portfolio and proprietary process know-how; management flags both patent expirations and technological obsolescence as threats. In a business where value is converted from IP into licensing and product premium, expiring or superseded patents directly erode pricing power and the out-licensing revenue stream.
- Management states that elevated energy prices and the inflation outlook raise the risk of higher PVA and other input costs. PVA is the core raw material for the Watersol film business, so the pass-through ability against fragmented competition determines segment margin.
- The importation of non-standard materials, including extruded films from China, continues to pressure competitive pricing in the mass-market segments the Company addresses - notably the embroidery film market it is targeting - capping realisations in the very segments intended to add volume.
- Management states currency volatility affects both export realisations and imported input costs. With distribution across Europe, Asia, North and South America and Africa and supply points in India, the UK and South America, the exposure is two-sided and structural.
- Working capital employed increased during the year, reflecting movement in receivables and inventory, and its normalisation continues to be a management focus - a cash-conversion drag on an otherwise debt-free balance sheet.
- Management names geopolitical developments among the factors that may cause operational fluctuations; the MD&A macro review points to a Middle East conflict that reset the global outlook, higher trade barriers, deeper geopolitical fragmentation and renewed trade tensions as dominant downside risks.
- Security products are supplied primarily to paper manufacturers and require specialised production capabilities, and the Company states it cannot disclose detail on the high-security business because of confidentiality requirements stipulated in its contracts. This limits both diversification and external verifiability of that revenue stream.
